tasks.title: Create Agent Module Directory Structure
tasks.description: Create the OpenEMR custom module skeleton for the AgentForge Clinical Co-Pilot with proper namespace registration and bootstrap file.
tasks.details:
Create directory structure:
```
interface/modules/custom_modules/oe-module-agentforge/
├── openemr.bootstrap.php
├── moduleConfig.php
├── src/
│   ├── Bootstrap.php
│   ├── Controllers/
│   ├── Services/
│   └── Events/
├── templates/
│   └── agent_panel.html.twig
├── public/
│   └── js/
└── tests/
```

The openemr.bootstrap.php should:
1. Register namespace 'OpenEMR\Modules\AgentForge\' using $classLoader->registerNamespaceIfNotExists()
2. Create Bootstrap instance with $eventDispatcher
3. Call $bootstrap->subscribeToEvents()

Follow pattern from oe-module-comlink-telehealth/openemr.bootstrap.php as reference.
tasks.testStrategy: Verify module loads without errors in OpenEMR dev environment. Check PHP error log for namespace registration issues. Confirm module appears in Administration > Modules list.

subtasks.title: Create base module directory structure and openemr.bootstrap.php
subtasks.description: Create the oe-module-agentforge directory under interface/modules/custom_modules/ with the openemr.bootstrap.php file that registers the namespace and initializes the Bootstrap class.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify module loads without PHP errors by checking PHP error log after accessing OpenEMR. Confirm namespace registration works by attempting to autoload a class from the src/ directory. Module should appear in Administration > Modules list when installed.

subtasks.title: Create src/Bootstrap.php with event subscription framework
subtasks.description: Create the Bootstrap.php class in src/ that handles module initialization, event dispatcher injection, and provides the subscribeToEvents() method for registering module event listeners.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify Bootstrap class instantiates without errors when module loads. Check that constructor properly initializes Twig environment and logger. Test getTemplatePath() and getURLPath() return valid paths.

subtasks.title: Create module subdirectory structure for Controllers, Services, and Events
subtasks.description: Create the src/Controllers/, src/Services/, and src/Events/ subdirectories following the established OpenEMR module patterns for organizing controller classes, service layer classes, and custom event definitions.
subtasks.details:
Create the following directory structure under src/:

```
src/
├── Controllers/     # For handling HTTP requests and UI interactions
│   └── .gitkeep
├── Services/        # For business logic and external API integrations  
│   └── .gitkeep
└── Events/          # For custom Symfony EventDispatcher events
    └── .gitkeep
```

These directories follow the patterns seen in oe-module-comlink-telehealth which has:
- Controller/ with TeleHealthCalendarController, TeleHealthVideoRegistrationController, etc.
- Services/ with TeleHealthProvisioningService, ParticipantListService, etc.
- Events/ with TelehealthNotificationSendEvent

Add .gitkeep files to empty directories to ensure they are tracked in git. The Controllers/ directory will hold AgentPanelController for the UI. Services/ will hold AgentService for LLM orchestration. Events/ will hold custom events for agent responses.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify all directories are created with correct permissions. Confirm .gitkeep files are present. Validate PSR-4 autoloading works for classes placed in these directories by creating a simple test class and attempting to instantiate it.

subtasks.title: Create templates directory with agent_panel.html.twig template
subtasks.description: Create the templates/ directory and the initial agent_panel.html.twig Twig template that will render the clinical co-pilot panel UI component.
subtasks.details:
Create templates/agent_panel.html.twig following Twig patterns from oe-module-comlink-telehealth/templates/: ```twig {# Agent Panel Template for Clinical Co-Pilot #}
{{ "Clinical Co-Pilot"|xlt }}
{# Chat messages will be rendered here #}
``` Note: OpenEMR uses the |xlt Twig filter for translations, as seen in the telehealth templates. The template uses Bootstrap 4.6 classes consistent with OpenEMR's frontend stack.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify Twig template syntax is valid by loading it through the Bootstrap's Twig environment. Check that xlt filter is available. Test template renders without errors when passed to Twig render() method.

subtasks.title: Create public/ and tests/ directories with placeholder files
subtasks.description: Create the public/ directory for static JavaScript assets and the tests/ directory for PHPUnit tests, including directory structure and placeholder files.
subtasks.details:
Create the following directory structure:

```
public/
├── js/
│   └── .gitkeep
└── index.php    # Entry point for module public pages

tests/
└── Tests/
    └── Unit/
        └── .gitkeep
```

Create public/index.php following pattern from oe-module-comlink-telehealth/public/index.php:
```php
<?php
declare(strict_types=1);

require_once dirname(__FILE__, 5) . '/globals.php';

use OpenEMR\Common\Csrf\CsrfUtils;

CsrfUtils::checkCsrfInput(INPUT_GET, dieOnFail: true);

// Module entry point - to be implemented
echo 'AgentForge Module';
```

The tests/ structure follows PHPUnit conventions and the OpenEMR test organization seen in oe-module-comlink-telehealth/tests/Tests/Unit/. The public/js/ directory will hold the frontend JavaScript for the agent panel interactions.
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify public/index.php is accessible via browser at /interface/modules/custom_modules/oe-module-agentforge/public/index.php (requires CSRF token). Confirm tests directory structure allows PHPUnit test discovery. Validate js/ directory exists for future asset placement.

subtasks.title: Create Bootstrap.php class with constructor and dependencies
subtasks.description: Create the Bootstrap.php file in interface/modules/custom_modules/oe-module-agentforge/src/ with PSR-4 namespace, constructor accepting EventDispatcherInterface, and required dependencies (LoggerInterface, OEGlobalsBag, module path initialization).
subtasks.details:
Following patterns from oe-module-comlink-telehealth/src/Bootstrap.php and oe-module-weno/src/Bootstrap.php:

1. Create src/Bootstrap.php with namespace OpenEMR\Modules\AgentForge
2. Constructor signature: __construct(private readonly EventDispatcherInterface $eventDispatcher, ?Kernel $kernel = null, ?LoggerInterface $logger = null)
3. Initialize module paths: $this->moduleDirectoryName = basename(dirname(__DIR__)), $this->modulePath = dirname(__DIR__), $this->installPath using OEGlobalsBag::getInstance()->getWebRoot()
4. Get logger via ServiceContainer::getLogger() fallback
5. Define MODULE_INSTALLATION_PATH and MODULE_NAME constants
6. Import: use OpenEMR\BC\ServiceContainer; use OpenEMR\Core\OEGlobalsBag; use Psr\Log\LoggerInterface; use Symfony\Contracts\EventDispatcher\EventDispatcherInterface;
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify class instantiates without errors when passed a mock EventDispatcherInterface. Check module path constants resolve correctly. Confirm logger is available via getter method.

subtasks.title: Implement subscribeToEvents() method with event listener registration
subtasks.description: Add the main subscribeToEvents() method that registers listeners for TwigEnvironmentEvent::EVENT_CREATED and PatientDemographics RenderEvent::EVENT_SECTION_LIST_RENDER_AFTER to inject the agent panel.
subtasks.details:
Following the telehealth and dashboard-context patterns:

1. Create subscribeToEvents(): void method
2. Register Twig template path listener: $this->eventDispatcher->addListener(TwigEnvironmentEvent::EVENT_CREATED, $this->addTemplateOverrideLoader(...))
3. Register patient demographics render listener: $this->eventDispatcher->addListener(RenderEvent::EVENT_SECTION_LIST_RENDER_AFTER, $this->renderAgentPanel(...))
4. Import: use OpenEMR\Events\Core\TwigEnvironmentEvent; use OpenEMR\Events\PatientDemographics\RenderEvent;
5. Use first-class callable syntax ($this->methodName(...)) for listener callbacks as seen in existing modules
6. Consider adding GlobalsInitializedEvent listener if module needs global settings
subtasks.testStrategy: Mock EventDispatcherInterface and verify addListener is called exactly twice with correct event names. Verify listener callbacks are valid callables.

subtasks.title: Implement addTemplateOverrideLoader() for Twig integration
subtasks.description: Add the TwigEnvironmentEvent handler that registers the module's template directory with the Twig FilesystemLoader so templates can be found.
subtasks.details:
Following oe-module-comlink-telehealth pattern:

1. Create addTemplateOverrideLoader(TwigEnvironmentEvent $event): void method
2. Get twig environment: $twig = $event->getTwigEnvironment()
3. Skip if it's the module's own twig instance (optional safety check)
4. Get loader and prepend path: if ($loader instanceof FilesystemLoader) { $loader->prependPath($this->getTemplatePath()); }
5. Create helper getTemplatePath(): string returning dirname(__DIR__) . DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR . 'templates' . DIRECTORY_SEPARATOR
6. Import: use Twig\Loader\FilesystemLoader;
7. This allows module templates to be discovered during rendering
subtasks.testStrategy: Create mock TwigEnvironmentEvent with mock FilesystemLoader. Verify prependPath is called with correct templates directory path. Test path resolution on filesystem.

subtasks.title: Implement renderAgentPanel() event handler with patient context check
subtasks.description: Add the PatientDemographics RenderEvent handler that checks for valid patient context and outputs the agent panel HTML/Twig template only on the patient summary page.
subtasks.details:
Following oe-module-weno renderWenoSection and oe-module-dashboard-context patterns:

1. Create renderAgentPanel(RenderEvent $event): void method
2. Get patient ID: $pid = $event->getPid() (RenderEvent constructor takes pid)
3. Early return if no pid: if (empty($pid)) { return; }
4. Optional: Check module configuration/globals to see if panel should display
5. Use logger for debugging: $this->logger->debug('AgentForge: Rendering panel', ['pid' => $pid])
6. Output HTML section using expand_collapse_widget() pattern or include template file
7. Import: use OpenEMR\Common\Session\SessionWrapperFactory; for session access if needed
8. Panel content will be implemented in later task - this establishes the injection point
subtasks.testStrategy: Mock RenderEvent with null pid - verify early return with no output. Mock with valid pid - verify HTML is output. Check logging occurs. Test ACL permission checks if implemented.

subtasks.title: Create openemr.bootstrap.php entry point and autoloader registration
subtasks.description: Create the openemr.bootstrap.php file that OpenEMR's module loader invokes, which registers the namespace with the classLoader and instantiates/subscribes the Bootstrap class.
subtasks.testStrategy: Navigate to patient summary page with module installed. Check PHP error log for namespace/class not found errors. Add temporary logging in subscribeToEvents and verify it fires on page load. Verify no performance degradation on page load timing.

subtasks.title: Implement chat panel container with patient context data attributes
subtasks.description: Add the main agentforge-panel div container with data-patient-id and data-session-token attributes using OpenEMR's Twig security filters (attr filter) for proper HTML attribute escaping.

Bind patient_id using {{ patient_id|attr }} filter as shown in templates/patient/partials/delete.html.twig and templates/oauth2/patient-select.html.twig patterns. tasks.title: Implement Agent Panel JavaScript Client
tasks.description: Create vanilla JS + jQuery client code for the agent chat panel with streaming response support and citation rendering.
tasks.testStrategy: Test message sending and receiving in browser console. Verify streaming chunks render progressively. Test citation formatting [encounter #X, date] renders as clickable links. Verify graceful handling when patient_id is missing.

subtasks.title: Create base AgentPanel module with initialization and configuration
subtasks.description: Create the foundational public/js/agent-panel.js file with IIFE module structure, state management, and initialization logic following OpenEMR's JS patterns (jQuery + vanilla JS hybrid approach).
subtasks.details:
Create public/js/agent-panel.js using an IIFE pattern like telehealth.js. The module should:

1. Use strict mode with (function($) { 'use strict'; ... })(jQuery) wrapper
2. Define AgentPanel object with state properties: patientId, sessionToken, conversationHistory[], isStreaming
3. Implement init() method that:
   - Reads panel data attributes: data-patient-id, data-session-token, data-csrf-token
   - Validates patient context exists (show error via showError() if missing)
   - Calls top.restoreSession() before any API calls (per OpenEMR pattern)
   - Binds DOM events via bindEvents()
4. Store CSRF token for API calls using csrf_token_form pattern from library/js/utility.js
5. Add error handling with showError(message) using asyncAlertMsg from utility.js or custom panel alert
6. Export to window.agentforge namespace (window.agentforge = window.agentforge || {}; window.agentforge.panel = AgentPanel)
7. Call init() on $(document).ready()
subtasks.testStrategy: Verify module loads without errors in browser console. Test init() detects missing patient context and shows error. Verify CSRF token and patient ID are correctly extracted from DOM data attributes. Test restoreSession() is called.

subtasks.title: Implement message sending with fetch API and streaming response handling
subtasks.description: Add sendMessage() method using fetch API with ReadableStream for processing SSE-style streaming responses from the /agentforge/turn endpoint.
subtasks.details:
Implement streaming message sending in AgentPanel:

1. Add sendMessage(userMessage) async method:
   - Call top.restoreSession() before fetch (required by OpenEMR session management)
   - Build request body: { patient_id, message, session_token }
   - POST to '/agentforge/turn' with headers: Content-Type: application/json, apicsrftoken
   - Set credentials: 'same-origin' for cookie-based auth

2. Implement streaming response processing:
   - Check response.ok and handle HTTP errors
   - Get reader via response.body.getReader()
   - Create TextDecoder('utf-8') for chunk processing
   - Process chunks in while loop: await reader.read()
   - Parse SSE-format lines (data: {json}\n\n)
   - Call processStreamChunk() for each parsed JSON object

3. Add processStreamChunk(chunk) handler:
   - Handle different chunk types: 'text', 'citation', 'error', 'done'
   - For 'text' chunks: append to current response via appendToResponse()
   - For 'citation' chunks: format and store in pendingCitations[]
   - For 'done': finalize response, store in conversationHistory
   - For 'error': display error message, reset streaming state

4. Implement state management: setStreaming(bool), getLastResponse()
subtasks.testStrategy: Test sendMessage with valid patient context. Mock streaming response to verify chunks process correctly. Verify error responses show appropriate messages. Test timeout handling. Verify CSRF token included in request headers.

subtasks.title: Implement chat UI rendering and message display components
subtasks.description: Build DOM manipulation methods for rendering chat messages, user inputs, and AI responses with proper HTML escaping using jsText/jsAttr from utility.js.
subtasks.details:
Create UI rendering methods for the chat panel:

1. Implement renderMessage(role, content, citations[]) method:
   - Create message container div with appropriate class: 'agent-message' or 'user-message'
   - Use jsText() from utility.js for HTML escaping content
   - For AI messages, process inline citation markers [N] and render citation links
   - Append to #agentforge-messages container
   - Auto-scroll to bottom of messages container

2. Add appendToResponse(textChunk) for streaming display:
   - Find or create current response element with .agent-response.streaming class
   - Append text using textContent (auto-escapes)
   - Use requestAnimationFrame for smooth updates
   - Update scroll position

3. Implement finalizeResponse() method:
   - Remove .streaming class from current response
   - Parse final content for citation markers
   - Render citation footer if citations exist
   - Store completed message in conversationHistory[]

4. Add showTypingIndicator() and hideTypingIndicator():
   - Display animated ellipsis while waiting for response
   - Remove on first chunk received

5. Implement clearChat() to reset conversation display
subtasks.testStrategy: Test message rendering with HTML special characters to verify escaping. Test streaming append updates DOM progressively. Verify auto-scroll works during streaming. Test typing indicator shows/hides correctly.

subtasks.title: Implement citation rendering with clickable encounter and record links
subtasks.description: Build citation formatting and rendering that converts citation references like [encounter #X, date] into clickable links that navigate to the referenced OpenEMR records.
subtasks.details:
Create citation handling subsystem:

1. Implement parseCitations(responseText, citationData[]) method:
   - Find citation markers in text: [1], [2], etc.
   - Map to citationData array from stream
   - Return processed text with citation spans

2. Create renderCitation(citation) for different citation types:
   - encounter: Build link to /interface/patient_file/encounter/encounter_top.php?set_encounter=X
   - medication: Link to medication view with Rx ID
   - lab: Link to lab results viewer
   - allergy: Link to allergy detail
   - Format: [Encounter #X, YYYY-MM-DD] or [Rx: drugname, date]

3. Implement renderCitationFooter(citations[]) method:
   - Group citations by type
   - Render numbered list with clickable links
   - Use xl() for translation of labels (if available)
   - Style with .citation-link class

4. Add click handler for citation links:
   - Use top.RTop.location for navigation (OpenEMR frame pattern) OR
   - Use dlgopen() from library/dialog.js for modal display
   - Pass proper parameters for patient context

5. Implement inlineCitationMarker(number, citation) for in-text rendering:
   - Create superscript link element
   - Tooltip with citation preview on hover
subtasks.testStrategy: Test citation parsing with various formats. Verify links navigate to correct OpenEMR pages. Test encounter links open proper encounter. Verify citation numbers match source data. Test with missing citation data gracefully degrades.

subtasks.title: Implement event bindings, keyboard handling, and error recovery
subtasks.description: Wire up all DOM event handlers including form submission, Enter key handling, error display, and graceful recovery from network failures or missing context.
subtasks.details:
Complete event handling and error recovery:

1. Implement bindEvents() method:
   - Bind form submit on #agentforge-form: e.preventDefault(), sendMessage()
   - Bind keydown on #agentforge-input: Enter key sends (Shift+Enter for newline)
   - Bind click on .agentforge-send-btn button
   - Bind click on #agentforge-clear for chat reset
   - Use jQuery's .on() for event delegation

2. Add input handling:
   - getUserInput(): get and clear input field value
   - disableInput(): disable during streaming
   - enableInput(): re-enable after response complete
   - Auto-resize textarea for multiline input

3. Implement error recovery:
   - handleNetworkError(error): show retry button, log to console
   - handleSessionExpired(): call top.restoreSession(), retry if possible
   - handleServerError(status, message): display user-friendly error
   - retryLastMessage(): re-send failed message

4. Add connection state management:
   - checkConnection(): validate session before sending
   - reconnect(): attempt to restore session if expired
   - Add abort controller for canceling in-flight requests

5. Implement graceful degradation:
   - Show fallback message if streaming not supported
   - Handle partial response recovery
   - Store pending message for retry
subtasks.testStrategy: Test Enter key sends message. Test Shift+Enter creates newline. Verify input disabled during streaming. Test error recovery shows retry option. Simulate network failure and verify graceful handling. Test abort controller cancels pending request.

tasks.title: Create Python Sidecar Project Structure

tasks.details:
Create sidecar/ directory at project root:
```
sidecar/
├── pyproject.toml
├── Dockerfile
├── src/
│   └── agentforge/
│       ├── __init__.py

subtasks.title: Create sidecar directory structure and pyproject.toml with dependencies
subtasks.description: Initialize the sidecar/ directory at project root with modern Python packaging using pyproject.toml including all required dependencies: FastAPI, uvicorn, pydantic-settings, langgraph, langchain, httpx, redis, langfuse, pyjwt.
subtasks.details:
Create sidecar/ directory at project root (/Users/sheep/Desktop/Gauntlet/openemr/sidecar/). Create pyproject.toml using modern Python packaging format (PEP 621):

```toml
[project]
name = "agentforge"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Clinical Co-Pilot agent sidecar for OpenEMR"
requires-python = ">=3.11"
dependencies = [
    "fastapi>=0.111.0",
    "uvicorn[standard]>=0.30.0",
    "pydantic-settings>=2.3.0",
    "langgraph>=0.1.0",
    "langchain>=0.2.0",
    "httpx>=0.27.0",
    "redis>=5.0.0",
    "langfuse>=2.35.0",
    "pyjwt>=2.8.0",
    "python-dotenv>=1.0.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.0.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23.0",
    "pytest-cov>=5.0.0",
    "ruff>=0.4.0",
    "mypy>=1.10.0",
    "httpx-sse>=0.4.0",
]

[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68", "wheel"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]
```

This follows the task's detailed directory structure requirements from ARCHITECTURE.md and matches the dependencies listed in the task description.
subtasks.testStrategy: Run 'pip install -e .' from sidecar/ directory and verify all dependencies install without conflicts. Verify pyproject.toml validates correctly with 'pip check'. Run 'python -c "import fastapi, langgraph, langfuse, redis, jwt, httpx"' to confirm all packages are importable.

subtasks.title: Create src/agentforge package structure with __init__.py files
subtasks.description: Create the src/agentforge/ package directory structure with all required subdirectories (gateway/, orchestrator/, tools/, verifier/, llm/, observability/) and __init__.py files for proper Python package initialization.
subtasks.details:
Create the following directory structure under sidecar/:

```
sidecar/
└── src/
    └── agentforge/
        ├── __init__.py           # Package marker, version info
        ├── gateway/
        │   └── __init__.py
        ├── orchestrator/
        │   └── __init__.py
        ├── tools/
        │   └── __init__.py
        ├── verifier/
        │   └── __init__.py
        ├── llm/
        │   └── __init__.py
        └── observability/
            └── __init__.py
```

The main __init__.py should contain:
```python
"""AgentForge Clinical Co-Pilot - FastAPI sidecar for OpenEMR."""
__version__ = "0.1.0"
```

Each subdirectory __init__.py should have a docstring describing its purpose per ARCHITECTURE.md:
- gateway: Auth gateway for JWT verification and sensitivity rules loading
- orchestrator: LangGraph multi-agent orchestration with parallel tool dispatch
- tools: Typed Python adapters over OpenEMR REST and FHIR R4 APIs

subtasks.title: Create Dockerfile for sidecar container with multi-stage build
subtasks.description: Build production-ready Dockerfile using multi-stage build pattern with Python 3.11, proper dependency installation, non-root user, and uvicorn as entrypoint following OpenEMR docker patterns.
subtasks.details:
Create sidecar/Dockerfile:
```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# AgentForge Clinical Co-Pilot sidecar service

# Build stage - install dependencies
FROM python:3.11-slim-bookworm AS builder

WORKDIR /app

# Install build dependencies
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Copy dependency files
COPY pyproject.toml .

# Create virtual environment and install dependencies
RUN python -m venv /opt/venv
ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir --upgrade pip && \
    pip install --no-cache-dir -e .

# Production stage
FROM python:3.11-slim-bookworm AS production

# Create non-root user (security)
RUN groupadd --gid 1000 agentforge && \
    useradd --uid 1000 --gid 1000 --create-home agentforge

WORKDIR /app

# Copy virtual environment from builder
COPY --from=builder /opt/venv /opt/venv
ENV PATH="/opt/venv/bin:$PATH"

# Copy application source
COPY --chown=agentforge:agentforge src/ ./src/
COPY --chown=agentforge:agentforge pyproject.toml .

# Install package in editable mode
RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -e .

USER agentforge

# Health check per ARCHITECTURE.md requirement
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=5s --start-period=10s --retries=3 \
    CMD curl -f http://localhost:8000/health || exit 1

EXPOSE 8000

ENTRYPOINT ["uvicorn", "agentforge.main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
```

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Literal
import jwt
from fastapi import HTTPException, Depends
from pydantic import BaseModel

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RequestContext:
    user_id: int
    patient_id: int
    role: str
    breakglass_flag: bool
    sensitivity_clearances: frozenset[str]

class AuthGateway:
    def __init__(self, redis_client, jwt_secret: str):
        self.redis = redis_client
        self.jwt_secret = jwt_secret
    
    async def validate_request(self, authorization: str) -> RequestContext:
        token = authorization.replace('Bearer ', '')
        payload = jwt.decode(token, self.jwt_secret, algorithms=['HS256'])
        
        if not payload.get('patient_id'):
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail='patient_id required')
        
        clearances = await self._load_clearances(payload['role'])
        
        return RequestContext(
            user_id=int(payload['sub']),
            patient_id=payload['patient_id'],
            role=payload['role'],
            breakglass_flag=payload.get('breakglass_flag', False),
            sensitivity_clearances=frozenset(clearances)
        )

subtasks.title: Implement JWT Validation Logic with Comprehensive Error Handling
subtasks.description: Create the JWT token validation component of AuthGateway that decodes HS256 tokens, validates expiration/signature, extracts claims, and raises appropriate HTTPExceptions for all failure modes.
subtasks.details:
Create src/agentforge/gateway/auth_gateway.py with JWT validation:

```python
import jwt
from jwt.exceptions import ExpiredSignatureError, InvalidSignatureError, DecodeError
from fastapi import HTTPException, Header
from typing import Any

class AuthGateway:
    def __init__(self, redis_client, jwt_secret: str):
        self.redis = redis_client
        self.jwt_secret = jwt_secret
        self.algorithm = 'HS256'
    
    def _validate_jwt(self, authorization: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Decode and validate JWT, returning payload or raising HTTPException."""
        if not authorization:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail='Authorization header required')
        
        if not authorization.startswith('Bearer '):
            raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail='Bearer token required')
        
        token = authorization[7:]  # Remove 'Bearer ' prefix
        
        try:
            payload = jwt.decode(
                token,
                self.jwt_secret,
                algorithms=[self.algorithm],
                options={'require': ['exp', 'sub', 'patient_id', 'role']}
            )
            return payload
        except ExpiredSignatureError:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail='Token expired')
        except InvalidSignatureError:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail='Invalid token signature')
        except DecodeError:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=401, detail='Malformed token')
        except jwt.MissingRequiredClaimError as e:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=f'Missing claim: {e.claim}')
```

Key requirements:
1. Use PyJWT library with HS256 algorithm matching PHP minting (Task 6)
2. Require claims: exp, sub (user_id), patient_id, role
3. Map all JWT exceptions to specific HTTP status codes (401 for auth failures, 400 for malformed requests)
4. Never expose internal exception details to client
5. Log validation failures with appropriate context for debugging

Use PyJWT to mint test tokens with known secret. Test with tokens from Task 6 PHP implementation to verify cross-language compatibility.

subtasks.title: Implement Redis Policy Loading with Fail-Closed Behavior and Caching
subtasks.description: Create the sensitivity clearance loading component that fetches role-based clearances from Redis policy table, implements fail-closed behavior returning 503 when policy is missing, and caches loaded clearances.
subtasks.details:
Extend src/agentforge/gateway/auth_gateway.py with Redis policy loading:

```python
import json
from typing import FrozenSet
from redis.asyncio import Redis
from redis.exceptions import RedisError

class AuthGateway:
    CLEARANCE_CACHE_TTL = 300  # 5 minutes local cache
    
    def __init__(self, redis_client: Redis, jwt_secret: str):
        self.redis = redis_client
        self.jwt_secret = jwt_secret
        self._clearance_cache: dict[str, tuple[float, frozenset[str]]] = {}
    
    async def _load_clearances(self, role: str) -> frozenset[str]:
        """Load sensitivity clearances from Redis. Fails closed on error."""
        # Check local cache first
        import time
        if role in self._clearance_cache:
            cached_time, clearances = self._clearance_cache[role]
            if time.time() - cached_time < self.CLEARANCE_CACHE_TTL:
                return clearances
        
        try:
            # Verify policy table is loaded (fail-closed gate)
            policy_loaded = await self.redis.get('sensitivity:loaded')
            if not policy_loaded:
                raise HTTPException(
                    status_code=503,
                    detail='Sensitivity policy not loaded - service unavailable'
                )
            
            # Load role-specific clearances
            clearance_data = await self.redis.hget('sensitivity:clearances', role)
            if clearance_data:
                clearances = frozenset(json.loads(clearance_data))
            else:
                # Role has no special clearances (default - minimal access)
                clearances = frozenset()
            
            # Update local cache
            self._clearance_cache[role] = (time.time(), clearances)
            return clearances
            
        except RedisError as e:
            # Redis failure = fail closed, return 503
            raise HTTPException(
                status_code=503,
                detail='Authorization service unavailable'
            )
```

Key requirements:
1. Check 'sensitivity:loaded' key exists before loading clearances (per Task 9)
2. Return 503 Service Unavailable when Redis is down or policy not loaded
3. Implement in-memory cache with 5-minute TTL to reduce Redis calls
4. Return empty frozenset for roles without explicit clearances (fail-closed)
5. Never log clearance values (could contain PHI-adjacent info)

Use redis-mock or fakeredis for unit tests. Integration test verifies coordination with Task 9 policy loader.

subtasks.title: Create Immutable RequestContext with Type-Safe Construction and FastAPI Dependency
subtasks.description: Build the frozen RequestContext dataclass and complete validate_request() method that assembles all components into a type-safe, immutable context object, plus FastAPI dependency for injection.
subtasks.details:
Complete src/agentforge/gateway/auth_gateway.py with RequestContext and FastAPI integration:

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import Depends, Header

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RequestContext:
    """Immutable context for an authenticated agent request.
    
    All fields are validated and parsed from JWT + Redis policy.
    Immutability prevents accidental mutation during request processing.
    """
    user_id: int
    patient_id: int
    role: str
    breakglass_flag: bool
    sensitivity_clearances: frozenset[str]
    session_id: str | None = None  # Set by session layer
    
    def has_clearance(self, clearance: str) -> bool:
        """Check if user has specific sensitivity clearance."""
        return clearance in self.sensitivity_clearances
    
    def can_access_sensitivity(self, required_clearances: set[str]) -> bool:
        """Check if user has ALL required clearances."""
        return required_clearances.issubset(self.sensitivity_clearances)

class AuthGateway:
    # ... JWT and Redis methods from subtasks 1-2 ...
    
    async def validate_request(
        self,
        authorization: str
    ) -> RequestContext:
        """Full request validation: JWT + Redis policy → RequestContext."""
        # 1. Validate JWT and extract claims
        payload = self._validate_jwt(authorization)
        
        # 2. Validate required fields with type safety
        try:
            user_id = int(payload['sub'])
            patient_id = int(payload['patient_id'])
            role = str(payload['role'])
            breakglass_flag = bool(payload.get('breakglass_flag', False))
        except (ValueError, TypeError) as e:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail='Invalid claim types')
        
        # 3. Load clearances from Redis (fail-closed)
        clearances = await self._load_clearances(role)
        
        # 4. Construct immutable context
        return RequestContext(
            user_id=user_id,
            patient_id=patient_id,
            role=role,
            breakglass_flag=breakglass_flag,
            sensitivity_clearances=clearances
        )

# FastAPI dependency for route injection
def get_auth_gateway() -> AuthGateway:
    from agentforge.config import get_settings
    from agentforge.storage.redis_client import get_redis
    settings = get_settings()
    return AuthGateway(get_redis(), settings.jwt_secret)

async def get_request_context(
    authorization: Annotated[str, Header()],
    gateway: Annotated[AuthGateway, Depends(get_auth_gateway)]
) -> RequestContext:
    """FastAPI dependency that validates request and returns context."""
    return await gateway.validate_request(authorization)
```

Key requirements:
1. Use @dataclass(frozen=True) for immutability - fields cannot be changed after creation
2. Use frozenset for clearances to prevent mutation
3. Add helper methods (has_clearance, can_access_sensitivity) for downstream use in tools
4. Type-check all claim conversions with explicit int()/str()/bool() casts
5. Create FastAPI Depends() compatible dependency for route injection
6. Session ID is optional - set by session layer after context creation

Integration test validate_request(): (1) full flow with valid JWT returns populated context, (2) invalid claim types return 400, (3) Redis failure returns 503. Test FastAPI dependency injection works in route handler. Verify RequestContext cannot be modified after creation by attempting field assignment.

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator
from typing import Literal

class BehavioralHealthRule(BaseModel):
    encounter_categories: list[str] = Field(min_length=1)
    required_clearances: list[str] = Field(min_length=1)

class SubstanceAbuseCFR42Rule(BaseModel):
    note_title_prefixes: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    note_types: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    required_clearances: list[str] = Field(min_length=1)
    description: str | None = None
    
    @field_validator('note_title_prefixes', 'note_types', mode='after')
    @classmethod
    def at_least_one_pattern(cls, v, info):
        # At least one of note_title_prefixes or note_types must be non-empty
        # This is validated at the model level
        return v

class AttendingOnlyRule(BaseModel):
    metadata_field: str
    metadata_value: int | str | bool
    required_clearances: list[str] = Field(min_length=1)
    description: str | None = None

class RecordClasses(BaseModel):
    behavioral_health: BehavioralHealthRule | None = None
    substance_abuse_cfr42: SubstanceAbuseCFR42Rule | None = None
    attending_only: AttendingOnlyRule | None = None

class SensitivityPolicy(BaseModel):
    version: int = Field(ge=1)
    role_clearances: dict[str, list[str]] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    record_classes: RecordClasses

subtasks.title: Implement policy_loader.py with YAML parsing and Redis population
subtasks.description: Create the policy loader module that reads the sensitivity policy YAML, validates it against Pydantic models, and populates Redis hash keys for runtime rule lookups by the Auth Gateway.
subtasks.details:
Create sidecar/src/agentforge/gateway/policy_loader.py:

```python
import json
import yaml
from pathlib import Path
from redis.asyncio import Redis
from pydantic import ValidationError
from .policy_models import SensitivityPolicy
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

class PolicyLoadError(Exception):
    """Raised when policy loading fails - triggers fail-closed behavior."""
    pass

async def load_sensitivity_policy(
    redis: Redis,
    config_path: str | Path,
    *,
    validate_only: bool = False
) -> SensitivityPolicy:
    """Load and validate sensitivity policy, populating Redis.
    
    Args:
        redis: Async Redis client
        config_path: Path to sensitivity_policy.yaml
        validate_only: If True, validate but don't write to Redis
        
    Returns:
        Validated SensitivityPolicy model
        
    Raises:
        PolicyLoadError: On YAML parse error, validation error, or Redis error
    """
    config_path = Path(config_path)
    
    if not config_path.exists():
        raise PolicyLoadError(f"Policy file not found: {config_path}")
    
    try:
        with open(config_path) as f:
            raw_policy = yaml.safe_load(f)
    except yaml.YAMLError as e:
        raise PolicyLoadError(f"Invalid YAML in {config_path}: {e}")
    
    if raw_policy is None:
        raise PolicyLoadError(f"Empty policy file: {config_path}")
    
    try:
        policy = SensitivityPolicy.model_validate(raw_policy)
    except ValidationError as e:
        raise PolicyLoadError(f"Policy validation failed: {e}")
    
    if validate_only:
        return policy
    
    # Populate Redis
    await _populate_redis(redis, policy)
    
    logger.info("Sensitivity policy loaded", extra={
        'version': policy.version,
        'record_classes': list(policy.record_classes.model_dump(exclude_none=True).keys()),
        'roles_configured': len(policy.role_clearances),
    })
    
    return policy

async def _populate_redis(redis: Redis, policy: SensitivityPolicy) -> None:
    """Populate Redis with policy data. All-or-nothing transaction."""
    pipe = redis.pipeline()
    
    # Clear existing policy data
    pipe.delete('sensitivity:rules', 'sensitivity:clearances', 'sensitivity:loaded')
    
    # Store record class rules
    for class_name, rules in policy.record_classes.model_dump(exclude_none=True).items():
        pipe.hset('sensitivity:rules', class_name, json.dumps(rules))
    
    # Store role-to-clearance mappings
    for role, clearances in policy.role_clearances.items():
        pipe.hset('sensitivity:clearances', role, json.dumps(clearances))
    
    # Set loaded flag with policy version
    pipe.set('sensitivity:loaded', str(policy.version))
    
    await pipe.execute()
```

Key design decisions per ARCHITECTURE.md §2:
- Use Redis pipeline for atomic all-or-nothing writes
- Store 'sensitivity:loaded' key that health check verifies (fail-closed)
- Never log rule contents (could reveal sensitivity categories)
- Use json.dumps for Redis hash values
- Support validate_only mode for dry-run checks

subtasks.title: Implement startup hook and health check integration
subtasks.description: Wire the policy loader into FastAPI application startup lifecycle and integrate with the health check endpoint to enforce fail-closed behavior when policy is not loaded.
subtasks.details:
Modify sidecar/src/agentforge/main.py to integrate policy loading on startup:

```python
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI, HTTPException
from agentforge.config import get_settings
from agentforge.gateway.policy_loader import load_sensitivity_policy, PolicyLoadError
from agentforge.storage.redis_client import get_redis_client
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    """Application lifespan - load policy on startup."""
    settings = get_settings()
    redis = await get_redis_client()
    
    try:
        policy = await load_sensitivity_policy(
            redis,
            settings.sensitivity_policy_path
        )
        app.state.sensitivity_policy_version = policy.version
        logger.info("Application startup complete with policy v%d", policy.version)
    except PolicyLoadError as e:
        logger.critical("CRITICAL: Sensitivity policy load failed - refusing to start", exc_info=e)
        # Exit with error - do not start without policy (fail-closed)
        raise SystemExit(1)
    
    yield
    
    # Cleanup on shutdown
    await redis.close()

app = FastAPI(
    title="AgentForge Clinical Co-Pilot",
    lifespan=lifespan
)

@app.get("/health")
async def health_check():
    """Health check - verifies sensitivity policy is loaded."""
    redis = await get_redis_client()
    
    policy_loaded = await redis.get('sensitivity:loaded')
    if not policy_loaded:
        raise HTTPException(
            status_code=503,
            detail="Sensitivity policy not loaded - service unavailable"
        )
    
    return {
        "status": "healthy",
        "policy_version": int(policy_loaded)
    }
```

async def check_record_visibility(
    self,
    ctx: RequestContext,
    record_metadata: RecordMetadata
) -> bool:
    """Check if user can access record based on metadata only.
    Never reads record content - only metadata fields.
    """
    rules = await self._get_sensitivity_rules()
    
    # Check behavioral health by encounter category
    if record_metadata.encounter_category in rules['behavioral_health']['encounter_categories']:
        if 'mental_health_authorized' not in ctx.sensitivity_clearances:
            return False
    
    # Check CFR42 by note type/title
    if self._matches_cfr42_pattern(record_metadata):
        if 'cfr42_authorized' not in ctx.sensitivity_clearances:
            return False
    
    # Check attending-only flag
    if record_metadata.attending_only:
        if not self._is_attending_or_supervisor(ctx, record_metadata):
            return False
    
    return True
```

Create src/agentforge/llm/client.py:

```python
from typing import Protocol, AsyncIterator
from dataclasses import dataclass

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Token:
    text: str
    finish_reason: str | None = None

class LLMClient(Protocol):
    async def stream(
        self,
        messages: list[dict],
        tools: list[dict] | None = None,
        max_tokens: int = 2048,
        timeout_s: float = 30.0,
    ) -> AsyncIterator[Token]: ...

class ClaudeClient(LLMClient):
    def __init__(self, api_key: str, model: str = 'claude-sonnet-4-20250514'):
        self.client = AsyncAnthropic(api_key=api_key)
        self.model = model
    
    async def stream(self, messages, tools=None, max_tokens=2048, timeout_s=30.0):
        async with self.client.messages.stream(
            model=self.model,
            messages=messages,
            tools=tools,
            max_tokens=max_tokens
        ) as stream:
            async for text in stream.text_stream:
                yield Token(text=text)
```

tasks.title: Implement LLM Provider Health Check and Failover
tasks.description: Create background health check system that monitors LLM provider status and handles failover to secondary provider.
tasks.details:
Create src/agentforge/llm/health_monitor.py:

```python
import asyncio
from enum import Enum

class ProviderStatus(Enum):
    HEALTHY = 'healthy'
    DEGRADED = 'degraded'
    DOWN = 'down'

class LLMHealthMonitor:
    def __init__(self, primary: LLMClient, secondary: LLMClient):
        self.primary = primary
        self.secondary = secondary
        self.primary_status = ProviderStatus.HEALTHY
        self.consecutive_failures = 0
    
    async def start_monitoring(self, interval_s: float = 30.0):
        while True:
            try:
                # Lightweight health check (not a full inference)
                await asyncio.wait_for(
                    self.primary.health_check(),
                    timeout=5.0
                )
                self.consecutive_failures = 0
                self.primary_status = ProviderStatus.HEALTHY
            except Exception:
                self.consecutive_failures += 1
                if self.consecutive_failures >= 2:
                    self.primary_status = ProviderStatus.DOWN
            
            await asyncio.sleep(interval_s)
    
    def get_active_client(self) -> LLMClient:
        if self.primary_status == ProviderStatus.DOWN:
            return self.secondary
        return self.primary
```

from typing import Literal, Any

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CitationRef:
    record_type: str  # 'encounter', 'prescription', 'lab_result', etc.
    record_id: str
    display_date: str
    display_label: str
    
    def to_citation_string(self) -> str:

class CitationBoundRecord:
    data: dict[str, Any]
    citation: CitationRef

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ToolResult:
    tool: str
    status: Literal['ok', 'timeout', 'error', 'empty', 'permission_denied']
    data: list[CitationBoundRecord] | None
    error: str | None
    latency_ms: int
    source_attribution: list[CitationRef]
```

class ActiveProblemsTool:
    async def execute(self, ctx: RequestContext) -> ToolResult:

            params={
                'patient': ctx.patient_id,
                'category': 'problem-list-item',
                'clinical-status': 'active'
            }

        # Parse FHIR Bundle, create CitationBoundRecords
        # Handle both coded (ICD/SNOMED) and free-text diagnoses
        records = []
        for entry in bundle['entry']:
            condition = entry['resource']
            records.append(CitationBoundRecord(
                data={
                    'code': condition.get('code', {}).get('coding', [{}])[0].get('code'),
                    'display': condition.get('code', {}).get('text') or condition.get('code', {}).get('coding', [{}])[0].get('display'),
                    'onset_date': condition.get('onsetDateTime'),
                    'clinical_status': condition.get('clinicalStatus', {}).get('coding', [{}])[0].get('code')
                },
                citation=CitationRef(record_type='condition', record_id=condition['id'], ...)
            ))
```

class ActiveMedicationsTool:
    async def execute(self, ctx: RequestContext) -> ToolResult:
        # Use FHIR MedicationRequest endpoint
        # CRITICAL: status=active filter is mandatory (AUDIT.md D3)
        # Soft-deleted meds must not appear
        
        resp = await client.get(
            f'{self.base_url}/apis/fhir/r4/MedicationRequest',
            params={
                'patient': ctx.patient_id,
                'status': 'active'  # MANDATORY - do not remove
            }
        )
        
        records = []
        for entry in bundle.get('entry', []):
            med_req = entry['resource']
            records.append(CitationBoundRecord(
                data={
                    'medication_name': self._extract_med_name(med_req),
                    'dose': self._extract_dosage(med_req),
                    'route': self._extract_route(med_req),
                    'frequency': self._extract_frequency(med_req),
                    'start_date': med_req.get('authoredOn'),
                    'prescriber': self._extract_prescriber(med_req)
                },
                citation=CitationRef(
                    record_type='prescription',
                    record_id=med_req['id'],
                    display_label=f"Rx: {self._extract_med_name(med_req)}"
                )
            ))

tasks.title: Implement get_recent_labs Tool Adapter
tasks.description: Create the most expensive tool adapter for lab results, joining procedure_order → procedure_report → procedure_result.
tasks.details:
Create src/agentforge/tools/labs.py:

```python
class RecentLabsTool:
    """Most expensive tool - requires composite index on OpenEMR tables.
    Pre-deploy requirement: indexes on (procedure_report_id, date) and 
    (procedure_order.patient_id, date_ordered).
    """
    
    async def execute(self, ctx: RequestContext, since: str | None = None) -> ToolResult:
        # Use FHIR Observation endpoint with category=laboratory
        params = {
            'patient': ctx.patient_id,
            'category': 'laboratory',
            '_sort': '-date',
            '_count': 50  # Limit to recent
        }
        if since:
            params['date'] = f'ge{since}'
        
        resp = await client.get(
            f'{self.base_url}/apis/fhir/r4/Observation',
            params=params
        )
        
        records = []
        for entry in bundle.get('entry', []):
            obs = entry['resource']
            records.append(CitationBoundRecord(
                data={
                    'test_name': obs.get('code', {}).get('text'),
                    'test_code': obs.get('code', {}).get('coding', [{}])[0].get('code'),
                    'value': self._extract_value(obs),
                    'unit': self._extract_unit(obs),
                    'reference_range': self._extract_range(obs),
                    'status': obs.get('status'),
                    'date': obs.get('effectiveDateTime')
                },
                citation=CitationRef(
                    record_type='lab_result',
                    record_id=obs['id'],
                    display_date=obs.get('effectiveDateTime', '')[:10]
                )
            ))
```

Note: This tool benefits most from Redis caching due to expensive join.

subtasks.description: Create _extract_value and _extract_unit helper methods to parse FHIR Observation valueQuantity, valueString, and valueCodeableConcept for different lab result types.
subtasks.details:
FHIR Observation resources store lab values in multiple formats per the FHIR spec:

1. Implement _extract_value(obs: dict) -> str | float | None method:
   - valueQuantity: Extract obs['valueQuantity']['value'] as float for numeric labs (e.g., glucose: 95.0)
   - valueString: Extract obs['valueString'] for text results (e.g., culture: 'No growth')
   - valueCodeableConcept: Extract obs['valueCodeableConcept']['text'] or coding[0]['display'] for coded results (e.g., positive/negative)
   - valueBoolean, valueInteger, valueRange, valueRatio: Handle additional FHIR value types
   - Return None if no value present (incomplete result)

2. Implement _extract_unit(obs: dict) -> str | None method:
   - Extract from obs['valueQuantity']['unit'] for numeric results
   - Handle UCUM codes vs display text
   - Return None for non-quantitative results

3. Per ARCHITECTURE.md §6 domain constraint #2: Lab values must match stored procedure_result value within tolerance - 'exact match to 2 decimal places for numeric values; verbatim for textual.' Preserve precision in extraction - do NOT round or format values.

4. Handle edge cases from OpenEMR's FhirObservationLabService:
   - result_text field when no structured value
   - abnormal_flag mapping to interpretation
   - units stored in procedure_result.units

Test coded extraction with valueCodeableConcept (positive/negative HIV). Test mixed bundle with all value types. Verify numeric precision preserved (95.00 stays 95.00, not 95). Test missing value returns None. Verify unit extraction handles UCUM codes.

subtasks.title: Implement Reference Range Parsing from FHIR Observation
subtasks.description: Create _extract_range helper method to parse FHIR Observation referenceRange with low/high/text values and interpretation codes for flagging abnormal results.
subtasks.details:
FHIR Observation stores reference ranges in the referenceRange array:

1. Implement _extract_range(obs: dict) -> dict | None method:
   - Extract from obs['referenceRange'][0] (typically single range)
   - Parse low: referenceRange.low.value with unit
   - Parse high: referenceRange.high.value with unit
   - Parse text: referenceRange.text for non-numeric ranges (e.g., 'Negative')
   - Return dict with keys: low, high, unit, text

2. Extract interpretation from obs['interpretation']:
   - Maps to abnormal_flag in procedure_result
   - Codes: N (normal), H (high), L (low), HH (critical high), LL (critical low), A (abnormal)
   - Store as interpretation field in CitationBoundRecord data

3. Handle OpenEMR-specific patterns from FhirObservationLabService.php:
   - range field format: 'low-high' text string
   - units may be separate from range
   - Some results have no reference range (normal is implicit)

4. Format for display while preserving raw values:
   - display_range: '65-99 mg/dL' for display
   - raw_low, raw_high: 65.0, 99.0 for verification

5. Per ARCHITECTURE.md §6 Verification Strategy: Stale data (labs >30 days when fresher expected) should be flagged inline. Include effectiveDateTime in CitationBoundRecord for staleness checking.

Test effectiveDateTime extraction for staleness checks.

subtasks.title: Implement Redis Caching Optimization for Expensive Lab Queries
subtasks.description: Implement aggressive Redis caching strategy for the expensive lab queries with cache key management, TTL optimization, and cache invalidation patterns.
subtasks.details:
Per ARCHITECTURE.md: 'This tool benefits most from Redis caching due to expensive join' across three tables. Implement:

1. Enhanced caching in execute() method:
   - Cache key: f'tool:recent_labs:{ctx.user_id}:{ctx.patient_id}:{args_hash}' where args_hash includes 'since' parameter
   - TTL: 60 seconds per ARCHITECTURE.md §3 Tool Dispatcher
   - Use Redis pipeline for atomic get/setex operations
   - Store serialized ToolResult via to_json() method from Task 13

2. Cache hit optimization:
   - Check cache BEFORE any HTTP call
   - Return ToolResult.from_cached(cached) immediately on hit
   - Track cache hits in latency_ms (should be <5ms)

3. Cache miss handling:
   - Execute FHIR query with full error handling
   - Parse response into CitationBoundRecord list
   - Serialize and store with setex (set with expiry)
   - Include cache miss indicator in Langfuse metrics

4. Assemble final CitationBoundRecord list:
   - Combine extracted data: test_name, test_code (from code.coding[0]), value, unit, reference_range, interpretation, status, date (effectiveDateTime)
   - Create CitationRef with record_type='lab_result', record_id=obs['id'], display_date from effectiveDateTime[:10]
   - Build source_attribution list from all citations

5. Return complete ToolResult:
   - tool='get_recent_labs'
   - status='ok' on success, 'empty' if no results, 'timeout'/'error' on failure
   - latency_ms from start to finish
   - source_attribution aggregating all CitationRefs

tasks.details:
Create src/agentforge/tools/vitals.py:

```python
class VitalsTrendTool:
    """Fetches vitals trend from form_vitals via internal endpoint.
    FHIR Observation covers vitals but our specific trend shape uses internal API.
    """
    
    async def execute(self, ctx: RequestContext, since: str | None = None) -> ToolResult:
        # Use internal endpoint for specific vitals trend shape
        resp = await client.get(
            f'{self.base_url}/agentforge/internal/vitals_trend',
            params={
                'patient_id': ctx.patient_id,
                'since': since or self._default_since()
            },
            headers={'Authorization': f'Bearer {ctx.jwt_token}'}
        )
        
        records = []
        for vitals in resp.json().get('vitals', []):
            records.append(CitationBoundRecord(
                data={
                    'date': vitals['date'],
                    'bps': vitals.get('bps'),  # systolic
                    'bpd': vitals.get('bpd'),  # diastolic
                    'pulse': vitals.get('pulse'),
                    'respiration': vitals.get('respiration'),
                    'temperature': vitals.get('temperature'),
                    'temp_method': vitals.get('temp_method'),
                    'height': vitals.get('height'),
                    'weight': vitals.get('weight'),
                    'bmi': vitals.get('BMI'),
                    'oxygen_saturation': vitals.get('oxygen_saturation')
                },
                citation=CitationRef(
                    record_type='vitals',
                    record_id=str(vitals['id']),
                    display_date=vitals['date'][:10]
                )
            ))
```

tasks.title: Implement get_recent_encounters Tool Adapter
tasks.description: Create tool adapter for fetching recent encounters with sensitivity filtering at the gateway level.
tasks.details:
Create src/agentforge/tools/encounters.py:

```python
class RecentEncountersTool:
    async def execute(self, ctx: RequestContext, since: str | None = None) -> ToolResult:
        # Use FHIR Encounter endpoint
        params = {
            'patient': ctx.patient_id,
            '_sort': '-date',
            '_count': 20
        }
        if since:
            params['date'] = f'ge{since}'
        
        resp = await client.get(
            f'{self.base_url}/apis/fhir/r4/Encounter',
            params=params
        )
        
        records = []
        for entry in bundle.get('entry', []):
            encounter = entry['resource']
            
            # Extract metadata for sensitivity check
            metadata = RecordMetadata(
                encounter_category=self._extract_category(encounter),
                record_type='encounter'
            )
            
            # Gateway checks visibility based on metadata only
            if not await self.gateway.check_record_visibility(ctx, metadata):
                continue  # Skip restricted encounters
            
            records.append(CitationBoundRecord(
                data={
                    'date': encounter.get('period', {}).get('start'),
                    'type': self._extract_type(encounter),
                    'reason': self._extract_reason(encounter),
                    'provider': self._extract_provider(encounter),
                    'location': self._extract_location(encounter)
                },
                citation=CitationRef(
                    record_type='encounter',
                    record_id=encounter['id'],
                    display_date=encounter.get('period', {}).get('start', '')[:10]
                )
            ))
```

Note: Sensitivity check happens on encounter category metadata, not encounter content.

subtasks.title: Implement RecordMetadata Extraction for Sensitivity Checking
subtasks.description: Create metadata extraction logic that extracts encounter category and record type from FHIR Encounter resources for gateway visibility decisions, ensuring no content is examined per ARCHITECTURE.md §2 security requirements.
subtasks.details:
Extend RecentEncountersTool with metadata extraction capability:

1. Define RecordMetadata dataclass (if not already in base module) with fields:
   - encounter_category: str | None (from form_encounter.pc_catid equivalent in FHIR)

2. Implement _extract_category(encounter) method that extracts encounter category from FHIR structure:

3. CRITICAL SECURITY CONSTRAINT: The metadata extraction must ONLY use structural fields (class, type codes), NEVER examine:

5. Create mapping dict for sensitivity-restricted encounter categories (from AUDIT.md S2, C4):
   - pc_catid values for behavioral health → 'mental_health'
   - pc_catid values for substance abuse (42 CFR Part 2) → 'cfr42'

subtasks.title: Integrate Gateway Visibility Checks with Filtering Loop
subtasks.description: Integrate the authorization gateway's check_record_visibility() method to filter encounters based on user clearances and encounter sensitivity metadata, ensuring restricted encounters are excluded before data extraction.
subtasks.details:
Complete the RecentEncountersTool integration with the gateway layer:

1. Add gateway dependency injection in constructor: def __init__(self, client: HttpClient, gateway: AuthorizationGateway, base_url: str)
2. In execute() method, for each encounter in the FHIR Bundle:
   a. FIRST extract RecordMetadata (encounter_category, record_type) using _extract_category()
   b. Call await self.gateway.check_record_visibility(ctx, metadata) with RequestContext and metadata
   c. If check returns False: skip this encounter entirely (continue), do NOT extract body data
   d. If check returns True: proceed with data extraction and CitationBoundRecord creation
3. Build CitationBoundRecord for allowed encounters:
   - data dict: date, type, reason, provider, location (extracted via helper methods)
   - citation: CitationRef with record_type='encounter', record_id=encounter['id'], display_date
4. Accumulate allowed records in records list, return as ToolResult.data
5. Handle edge cases:
   - All encounters filtered → return ToolResult with status='ok', data=[] (empty but authorized)
   - Some filtered → return partial list with only authorized encounters
6. Log visibility check results for debugging (without PHI - just counts: 'Filtered X of Y encounters')
7. Implement source_attribution list from all allowed CitationRef objects for ToolResult
8. This is the first tool implementing record visibility checks - establish the pattern for subsequent tools (notes, labs)

tasks.title: Implement get_recent_notes Tool Adapter
tasks.description: Create tool adapter for clinical notes from pnotes + form_clinical_notes with sensitivity-aware filtering.
tasks.details:
Create src/agentforge/tools/notes.py:

```python
class RecentNotesTool:
    async def execute(self, ctx: RequestContext, since: str | None = None) -> ToolResult:
        # Use internal endpoint that joins pnotes + form_clinical_notes
        resp = await client.get(
            f'{self.base_url}/agentforge/internal/recent_notes',
            params={
                'patient_id': ctx.patient_id,
                'since': since
            }
        )
        
        records = []
        for note in resp.json().get('notes', []):
            # Check sensitivity based on note metadata only
            metadata = RecordMetadata(
                note_type=note.get('note_type'),
                note_title=note.get('title'),
                attending_only=note.get('attending_only', False)
            )
            
            if not await self.gateway.check_record_visibility(ctx, metadata):
                # Return permission_denied for this specific note
                records.append(CitationBoundRecord(
                    data={'status': 'permission_denied', 'note_type': note.get('note_type')},
                    citation=CitationRef(record_type='note', record_id=str(note['id']), ...)
                ))
                continue
            
            records.append(CitationBoundRecord(
                data={
                    'date': note['date'],
                    'type': note['note_type'],
                    'author': note['author'],
                    'title': note.get('title'),
                    'content': note['body']  # Only fetched after sensitivity check passes
                },
                citation=CitationRef(record_type='note', record_id=str(note['id']), ...)
            ))
```

subtasks.title: Implement Permission-Denied Status Handling in Results
subtasks.description: Add permission_denied status handling that returns redacted CitationBoundRecord entries for restricted notes, preserving citation references while hiding content.
subtasks.details:
Implement permission-denied pattern unique to notes tool (differs from encounters which silently filter):

1. When gateway.check_record_visibility() returns False for a note, create a redacted CitationBoundRecord:
   ```python
   CitationBoundRecord(
       data={
           'status': 'permission_denied',
           'note_type': metadata.note_type,  # Safe to include type
           'date': note.get('date'),  # Safe to include date
           'reason': 'Restricted access'  # Generic reason, never specific
       },
       citation=CitationRef(
           record_type='note',
           record_id=str(note['id']),
           display_date=note.get('date'),
           display_label=f"Note #{note['id']} (restricted)"
       )
   )
   ```

2. Permission-denied records are INCLUDED in the results list (not filtered out) so:
   - The LLM knows restricted notes exist for this patient
   - The synthesizer can say 'some notes are restricted from your view'
   - Audit trail shows which notes were denied (without exposing content)

3. Track denied note count in ToolResult metadata: denied_count=N

4. The permission_denied status enables the verifier to handle claims about restricted notes:
   - If LLM claims 'patient has no substance abuse history' but permission_denied notes exist, verifier flags potential counterfactual

5. Log denied access decisions for audit (note ID only, no content): 'Access denied for note {note_id} to user {user_id}'

subtasks.title: Implement Two-Phase Note Body Fetching After Sensitivity Pass
subtasks.description: Complete the two-phase fetch pattern where note body content is only retrieved AFTER metadata-based sensitivity check passes, preventing any content exposure for restricted notes.
subtasks.details:
Implement the critical two-phase fetch security pattern:

1. Phase 1 (already implemented in subtask 1): Fetch metadata from internal endpoint
   - Internal endpoint returns: id, source, date, author, title, note_type, category, attending_only
   - Body/content is NOT included in Phase 1 response

2. Phase 2 (this subtask): Fetch body only for authorized notes
   - After check_record_visibility() passes, make secondary request for body:
   ```python
   body_resp = await client.get(
       f'{self.base_url}/agentforge/internal/note_body',
       params={'note_id': note['id'], 'source': note['source']}
   )
   ```
   - OR: Internal endpoint returns body field but tool only accesses it post-check

3. Build CitationBoundRecord for allowed notes:
   ```python
   CitationBoundRecord(
       data={
           'date': note['date'],
           'type': note['note_type'],
           'author': note['author'],
           'title': note.get('title'),
           'content': body_content,  # Only populated AFTER sensitivity pass
           'source': note['source']  # pnote or clinical_note
       },
       citation=CitationRef(
           record_type='note',
           record_id=str(note['id']),
           display_date=note.get('date'),
           display_label=f"Note: {note.get('title', 'Untitled')} ({note['date']})"
       )
   )
   ```

4. SECURITY INVARIANT: Code structure must make it impossible to access body before check:
   - Use separate method _fetch_authorized_body(note_id, source) that's only called in the if-allowed branch
   - Add assertion/guard: if not visibility_passed: raise SecurityViolation('Body access before authorization')

5. Build source_attribution list from all CitationRef objects (both allowed and denied)

6. Return ToolResult with mixed allowed/denied records, latency_ms, and denied_count metadata
subtasks.testStrategy: Critical security tests: (1) Test body is NEVER accessed for denied notes - mock client and verify no body endpoint called for restricted notes, (2) Test body IS fetched for allowed notes - verify body endpoint called, (3) Test execution order: visibility check BEFORE body fetch (add timing assertions), (4) Test complete CitationBoundRecord structure for allowed notes includes all fields, (5) Test source_attribution includes citations from both allowed and denied notes, (6) End-to-end test: user without CFR42 clearance requests notes from patient with substance abuse notes - verify no body content exposed for restricted notes, body visible for unrestricted notes, (7) Performance test: verify Phase 2 body fetches run in parallel for allowed notes

subtasks.title: Implement UNION Query for pnotes and form_clinical_notes Tables
subtasks.description: Build the SQL UNION ALL query that combines notes from both pnotes and form_clinical_notes tables with normalized column selection.
subtasks.details:
Create the UNION query structure that joins both tables:

1. **pnotes table query component:**
   - Select columns: `'pnote' as source, id, date, user as author, title, body`
   - Add NULL placeholders for clinical note-specific fields: `NULL as note_type, NULL as attending_only`
   - Filter by: `pid = ? AND date >= ? AND deleted != 1` (matches existing pnotes.inc.php pattern)

2. **form_clinical_notes table query component:**
   - Select columns: `'clinical_note' as source, id, date, user as author, codetext as title, description as body`
   - Include clinical-specific fields: `clinical_notes_type as note_type, attending_only`
   - Filter by: `pid = ? AND date >= ? AND activity = 1` (matches ClinicalNotesService.php pattern line 203)

3. **Combined query:**
   - Use UNION ALL (not UNION) to preserve duplicates and improve performance
   - Apply ORDER BY date DESC and LIMIT 50 to the combined result
   - Use parameterized query with `[$patientId, $since, $patientId, $since]` bindings

4. **Implementation location:** Add `recentNotes()` method to src/Controllers/InternalApiController.php

5. **Use QueryUtils::fetchRecords()** for execution (per library/pnotes.inc.php:205 pattern)

subtasks.title: Implement Deleted/Inactive Filtering and Metadata Extraction
subtasks.description: Add filtering logic for deleted/inactive notes and extract metadata for sensitivity checking without exposing full note body initially.
subtasks.details:
Implement filtering and metadata extraction layer:

1. **Filtering logic (embedded in SQL, see subtask 1):**
   - pnotes: `deleted != 1` excludes soft-deleted notes (per library/pnotes.inc.php:28,177,239)
   - form_clinical_notes: `activity = 1` includes only active records (per src/Services/ClinicalNotesService.php:27-28)

2. **Create formatNotes() helper method:**
   ```php
   private function formatNotes(array $notes): array {
       return array_map(function ($note) {
           return [
               'id' => (int) $note['id'],
               'source' => $note['source'],
               'date' => $note['date'],
               'author' => $note['author'],
               'title' => $note['title'],
               'has_body' => !empty($note['body']),
               'note_type' => $note['note_type'],
               'attending_only' => (bool) $note['attending_only'],
               // body intentionally omitted - fetched on demand
           ];
       }, $notes);
   }
   ```

3. **Sensitivity metadata extraction:**
   - Return `attending_only` flag for clinical notes (indicates restricted access)
   - Return `note_type` to allow client-side filtering/display decisions
   - Omit `body` field in initial response (fetched separately to control access)

4. **Add input validation:**
   - Validate `patient_id` is a positive integer
   - Validate `since` is a valid ISO 8601 datetime string
   - Return 400 error for invalid parameters

subtasks.title: Implement JWT Validation and Audit Logging Integration
subtasks.description: Add validateAgentJwt() authentication check and integrate EventAuditLogger for access tracking per OpenEMR security requirements.
subtasks.details:
Implement security layer for the endpoint:

1. **JWT Validation (at method entry):**
   - Call `$this->validateAgentJwt($request)` before any database access
   - This method should verify the agent JWT token from Authorization header
   - Throw appropriate HTTP 401/403 exception if validation fails
   - Extract agent identity from validated token for audit logging

2. **Audit Logging Integration:**
   ```php
   use OpenEMR\Common\Logging\EventAuditLogger;
   
   // After successful query, before returning response:
   EventAuditLogger::instance()->newEvent(
       'patient-record',           // event type (per LOG_TABLES mapping)
       $agentIdentity,             // user from JWT
       'agent',                    // groupname
       1,                          // success=1
       'Agent API: Retrieved recent notes',  // comments

Create src/agentforge/tools/search_notes.py:

```python
class SearchNotesTool:
    """Powers UC-2 (contraindication query). Uses MySQL FULLTEXT.
    v1: FULLTEXT on pnotes.body and form_clinical_notes.note
    Production: migrate to OpenSearch for scale.
    """
    
    async def execute(self, ctx: RequestContext, query: str) -> ToolResult:
        start = time.monotonic()
        
        resp = await client.get(
            f'{self.base_url}/agentforge/internal/search_notes',
            params={
                'patient_id': ctx.patient_id,
                'query': query,
                'limit': 5
            }
        )
        
        latency_ms = int((time.monotonic() - start) * 1000)
        
        if latency_ms > 1000:
            # Flag slow search but don't block
            records = resp.json().get('results', [])
            return ToolResult(
                tool='search_notes',
                status='ok',
                data=[self._to_citation_bound(r) for r in records],
                error='Search took longer than expected',
                latency_ms=latency_ms,
                source_attribution=[...]
            )
        
        records = resp.json().get('results', [])
        return ToolResult(
            tool='search_notes',
            status='ok' if records else 'empty',
            data=[self._to_citation_bound(r) for r in records] or None,
            latency_ms=latency_ms,
            source_attribution=[...]
        )
```

```php
public function searchPatientNotes(int $patientId, string $query, int $limit = 5): array
{
    $limit = min($limit, self::MAX_LIMIT);
    
    $sql = "
        SELECT id, 'pnotes' AS source_table, date, title, 
               MATCH(body) AGAINST (? IN NATURAL LANGUAGE MODE) AS relevance_score,
               SUBSTRING(body, 1, ?) AS snippet
        FROM pnotes
        WHERE pid = ? AND MATCH(body) AGAINST (? IN NATURAL LANGUAGE MODE)
        
        UNION ALL
        
        SELECT id, 'clinical_notes' AS source_table, date, codetext AS title,
               MATCH(description) AGAINST (? IN NATURAL LANGUAGE MODE) AS relevance_score,
               SUBSTRING(description, 1, ?) AS snippet
        FROM form_clinical_notes
        WHERE pid = ? AND MATCH(description) AGAINST (? IN NATURAL LANGUAGE MODE)
        
        ORDER BY relevance_score DESC
        LIMIT ?
    ";
    
    return QueryUtils::fetchRecords($sql, [
        $query, self::MAX_SNIPPET_LENGTH, $patientId, $query,
        $query, self::MAX_SNIPPET_LENGTH, $patientId, $query,
        $limit
    ]);
}
```

tasks.title: Implement LangGraph Orchestrator
tasks.description: Create the multi-agent orchestrator using LangGraph for parallel tool dispatch within the 4s tool-phase budget.
tasks.details:
Create src/agentforge/orchestrator/graph.py:

```python
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END
from langgraph.prebuilt import ToolExecutor
from typing import TypedDict, Annotated
import asyncio

class AgentState(TypedDict):
    user_message: str
    conversation_memory: list[dict]
    plan: dict | None
    tool_results: dict[str, ToolResult]
    synthesis: str
    verified_claims: list[str]

def create_agent_graph(tools: dict, llm_client: LLMClient):
    graph = StateGraph(AgentState)
    
    graph.add_node('planner', planner_node)
    graph.add_node('tool_dispatcher', tool_dispatcher_node)
    graph.add_node('synthesizer', synthesizer_node)
    graph.add_node('verifier', verifier_node)
    
    graph.set_entry_point('planner')
    graph.add_edge('planner', 'tool_dispatcher')
    graph.add_edge('tool_dispatcher', 'synthesizer')
    graph.add_edge('synthesizer', 'verifier')
    graph.add_edge('verifier', END)
    
    return graph.compile()

async def tool_dispatcher_node(state: AgentState, tools: dict):
    """Dispatch up to 3 tools in parallel. 4s total budget."""
    plan = state['plan']
    tool_calls = plan['tool_calls']
    
    semaphore = asyncio.Semaphore(3)  # Max 3 concurrent
    results = {}
    
    async def execute_with_limit(tool_name: str, args: dict):
        async with semaphore:
            return await tools[tool_name].execute(**args)
    
    tasks = [
        asyncio.create_task(execute_with_limit(tc['name'], tc['args']))
        for tc in tool_calls
    ]
    
    # 4s total budget
    done, pending = await asyncio.wait(tasks, timeout=4.0)
    for task in pending:
        task.cancel()
    
    return {'tool_results': results}
```

from enum import Enum

class UseCase(Enum):
    UC1_ADMIT_SYNTHESIS = 'admit_synthesis'
    UC2_CONTRAINDICATION = 'contraindication'
    UC3_DELTA_COMPUTATION = 'delta_computation'
    UC4_FOLLOWUP = 'followup'

PLANNER_PROMPT = '''
You are a clinical query planner. Given a user message about a patient,
determine the use case and required tools.

Use cases:
- UC1 (admit_synthesis): "give me a summary", "what do I need to know"
- UC2 (contraindication): "is there a contraindication", "can I give X"
- UC3 (delta_computation): "what changed since last visit"
- UC4 (followup): follow-up to a previous question

Output JSON:
{
  "use_case": "UC1",
  "tool_calls": [
    {"name": "get_demographics", "args": {}},
    {"name": "get_active_problems", "args": {}}
  ],
  "parallel_batches": [["get_demographics", "get_active_problems", "get_active_medications"], ["get_allergies", "get_recent_labs"]]
}
'''

async def planner_node(state: AgentState, llm: LLMClient) -> dict:
    # Use cheaper model (4o-mini tier) for planning
    response = await llm.generate(
        messages=[{'role': 'system', 'content': PLANNER_PROMPT},
                  {'role': 'user', 'content': state['user_message']}],
        response_format={'type': 'json_object'}
    )
    
    plan = json.loads(response)
    return {'plan': plan}
